raw_response:
I've been farming these 12 mu in Quzhou for 30 years now — I'm 50, finished middle school, and this is what I know. It's just me and my wife at home. Our son works in Shijiazhuang and sends money sometimes, but I don't plan the farm around that. I have 10 mu in wheat-maize and 2 mu of cotton by the well. I've thought about dropping the cotton — it's heavy work and we're not getting younger — but the price last year was alright, and 2 mu won't kill us. Still, with only two of us, every decision is about whether we can physically do it and whether we have the cash.

For wheat, I plant in early October around the 10th. I use Jimai 22, same as my neighbor Lao Zhang. Seed is about 35 yuan per mu. The extension fellow says I should soil-test, but I've farmed this land long enough. I put down 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that's the base. Then in late March when the wheat joints, I topdress with another 50 jin of urea per mu. The extension guy says 15 kg nitrogen per mu is enough, and that's about what I do. I won't cut back — two years ago I tried less topdress and the wheat went yellow. Lost money. I irrigate three times: winter irrigation if it's dry, jointing, and heading. Water costs more now with the meters, but dry wheat is worse than a water bill.

Maize is the rush job. Harvest wheat in early June, and I have maybe five days to get maize in the ground before I lose yield. I hire a combine for wheat and a no-till planter for maize — no time for plowing. Hybrid seed, about 45 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer down at planting and topdress urea at jointing. Total nitrogen around 14 kg per mu, a bit less than wheat. I irrigate twice if July turns hot — at the big trumpet stage and at silking. If the rains come, maybe once is enough.

The cotton on that 2 mu, I plant late April after plowing and making ridges. Improved Bt seed, about 30 yuan per mu. I use less fertilizer than wheat — about 12 kg nitrogen per mu, split between base and when it flowers. Two irrigations. Herbicide once, insecticide two or three times even with Bt. The real cost is picking. Me and my wife can do the early picks, but come September I'll hire two women from the village for a week. That's money out the door, but without it the cotton stays in the field.

This year I need about 8,600 yuan for all inputs, water, chemicals, and hired labor. That's nearly all my cash. I thought about borrowing less from my brother-in-law, but I've learned that saving 300 yuan on fertilizer and losing 500 yuan in grain is a fool's bargain. Better to sleep with an empty pocket than an empty stomach. If the weather holds, I expect about 420 kg per mu from wheat, 480 from maize, and 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.
